title: The equivalence principle and local flatness
summary: Freely falling frames as the generalisation of inertial frames; weak, Einstein and strong equivalence principles; gravitational redshift and time dilation; local flatness by counting degrees of freedom, with the twenty-component deficit that will be curvature. The first unit in which spacetime is allowed to be curved.

objectives.description: Objectives will be finalised when the unit is prepared; the source material is 8.962 Lectures 6–7 (Lecture Guide pages 1–2 and the recorded lectures), Tong Sections 1.2.4–1.2.5 and Carroll Chapter 4.

preparation.description: Read the Lecture Guide's synopsis of Lectures 6 and 7 on the equivalence principle (PDF page 1, final paragraphs).
Read the Lecture Guide's continuation of Lecture 7 (PDF page 2): the counting argument for local flatness and the twenty leftover constraints.
Watch Lecture 6: The Principle of Equivalence and Lecture 7: The Principle of Equivalence Continued; Parallel Transport (first half), from the video gallery.
Second account: Tong, General Relativity, Section 1.2 (1.2.4 The Equivalence Principle, 1.2.5 Gravitational Time Dilation), reference-only.
Optional: Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, Chapter 4 Gravitation (opening sections on the equivalence principle), reference-only.
